english: Let $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ be an arithmetic progression of real numbers such that $a_1a_2=10$, $a_2a_3=40$ and $a_3a_4=88$. Then the value of $\left|a_{12}\right|$ is ______.
hindi: माना $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ वास्तविक संख्याओं की एक समान्तर श्रेढ़ी है, जिसके लिए $a_1a_2=10$, $a_2a_3=40$ तथा $a_3a_4=88$ है। तब $\left|a_{12}\right|$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Let $d$ be the common difference. For any $n$, $a_{n+1}a_{n+2}-a_na_{n+1}=a_{n+1}(a_{n+2}-a_n)=a_{n+1}\cdot2d$.
So the products of consecutive terms have differences that again form an arithmetic progression: $2d\,a_2,\ 2d\,a_3,\dots$ with common difference $2d\cdot d=2d^2$.
If $d=-3$: $a_2=-5$, $a_1=-2$, $a_3=-8$, $a_4=-11$; the products are the same.
originality_note: New: an AP is recovered from the products of consecutive terms; the operation 'product of neighbours' turns the AP into a sequence whose differences form an AP with common difference 2d^2 (way 5: operation on AP terms linked to the AP itself). Closest known: 'sum of four consecutive AP terms is 32 and the product of the middle two is 60'. Different because: only the three neighbour products are given, d is found from their second difference, and the sign ambiguity is removed by asking for |a_12|.
blueprint_concepts: Operations on terms of an AP

concept_use.Arithmetic Progression (AP) & Sum of AP: a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d gives a_12 = a_1 + 11d once a_1 and d are known.
concept_use.Operations on terms of an AP: The products a_n a_{n+1} have consecutive differences 2d a_{n+1}, whose own difference 2d^2 gives d^2 = 9.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and progression is introduced before use, all conditions are stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (sympy/fractions or brute force), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Asked for |a_12| because a and -a give the same products. Changed: No change.
key_step: Seeing that differences of neighbour products are 2d a_{n+1}, so their difference is 2d^2.
justification: Routine chain of three steps with one light observation; numerical but short. Level 2 like 2023-P2-Q9 (L2).
